notes: No advertised tool is shown as gated by a flag, capability, toolset, environment variable, URL path, or header in the supplied source; all advertised tools are treated as default-enabled.

add_calendar_event_participants.rationale: The implementation mutates the selected event's `participants` and returns the event, exposing non-public calendar data that may include third-party-authored event fields. The tool docstring advertises that it will email new participants, which raises a SINK label even though the shown implementation only appends participants.

append_to_file.rationale: Appends agent-supplied `content` to a selected cloud-drive file and returns the file, exposing non-public file content. Files can be third-party/shared documents, so returned `filename`, `content`, and owner-related identifiers may be untrusted. Writing to a cloud file selected by `file_id` can place agent-supplied content into a record readable by collaborators, including external owners/shared users, making it a sink.

cancel_calendar_event.rationale: Cancels the selected event and calls `inbox.send_email` to notify that event's `participants`, attaching the event. The chosen `event_id` determines which calendar record is changed and which participant addresses receive the notification.

create_calendar_event.rationale: Creates a calendar event from agent-supplied fields and sends an invitation email to agent-supplied `participants` with `subject`, `body`, and the new event attached, making it a message sink.

create_file.rationale: Creates a new file in the user's cloud drive from agent-supplied `filename` and `content` and returns the new file. The code does not show that the newly created file is shared with an attacker-readable destination by default.

delete_email.rationale: `delete_email` mutates the user's inbox by moving the selected email from `emails` to `trash`; the wrapper returns only a fixed success string containing the supplied `email_id`, not email contents.

delete_file.rationale: Deletes a selected cloud-drive file and returns the deleted `CloudDriveFile`, including non-public file contents. Because the drive can contain shared/third-party-owned files, returned file fields may include untrusted author-controlled text and identifiers.

get_current_day.rationale: Returns only `calendar.current_day.isoformat()`, a date value from the calendar object, with no attacker-authored text and no outbound delivery.

get_day_calendar_events.rationale: Returns events from the user's calendar for a day, exposing non-public calendar data. Some calendar event text/participants may come from outside parties, as shown by the externally addressed event in the workspace data.

get_draft_emails.rationale: Returns draft emails in the user's inbox account; drafts are non-public user account data. The code does not show third-party authorship of drafts.

get_file_by_id.rationale: Returns a cloud-drive file by id, including its content and sharing metadata, which are non-public account data. Shared/third-party-owned files can have outside-authored `filename`, `content`, and `owner` fields.

get_received_emails.rationale: Returns received emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. Received messages' `sender`, `subject`, and `body` are authored by outside senders and are therefore untrusted.

get_sent_emails.rationale: Returns sent emails stored in the user's inbox account, including recipients, subject, body, and attachments, which are non-public account data.

get_unread_emails.rationale: Returns unread emails from the user's inbox, which are non-public account data. `get_unread` also marks them read. Received emails include attacker-/third-party-authored `sender`, `subject`, and `body` fields, as shown by external unread messages in the workspace data.

list_files.rationale: Lists all cloud-drive files visible in the user's account, including non-public file contents and metadata. Some visible files are externally owned or shared, so returned file text and identifiers can be untrusted.

reschedule_calendar_event.rationale: Updates a selected calendar event, emails its `participants` about the reschedule with the event attached, and returns the event. The returned event is non-public calendar data and may contain third-party-authored event text/participants.

search_calendar_events.rationale: Searches the user's calendar and returns event details, which are non-public account data. Calendar events can include third-party/invitation content, including externally originated phishing-like event text in the workspace data, so returned `title`, `description`, `location`, and participant identifiers can be untrusted.

search_contacts_by_email.rationale: Returns contacts from the user's email account. Since contacts are populated from email senders/recipients and names are derived from addresses, outside senders can cause attacker-chosen contact `email` and `name` values to be returned.

search_contacts_by_name.rationale: The contact list is derived from the user's email account and returned by search. Contacts are created from email participants including external received-message senders, and `name` is derived from the email address local part, so attacker-controlled sender addresses can determine returned `email` and `name`.

search_emails.rationale: Searches and returns emails from the user's inbox account, so it can return non-public email data. Because the searched set can include received emails, outside senders can author returned `sender`, `subject`, and `body` values.

search_files.rationale: Searches cloud-drive file contents and returns matching file objects, exposing non-public file contents and metadata. Files may be externally owned/shared, so returned `filename`, `content`, and owner identifiers can be untrusted.

search_files_by_filename.rationale: Searches the user's cloud drive and returns matching file objects including contents, which are non-public account data. The drive includes shared/third-party-owned files, so file names, contents, and owner identifiers can be attacker- or third-party-authored.

send_email.rationale: `send_email` accepts agent-supplied `recipients`, `cc`, `bcc`, `subject`, `body`, and `attachments`, constructs a sent `Email`, and stores/sends it via `inbox.send_email(...)`; the recipient fields are agent-chosen addresses, so this is a message sink.

share_file.rationale: Adds an agent-supplied `email` to a file's `shared_with` permissions and returns the file. Sharing a selected file to an agent-chosen address is a sink for that file's contents. The returned file is non-public cloud-drive data and can be third-party-authored if the selected file is shared/external.
